title: Personal Credit Cards: Billing Disputes on Posted Charges
content:
A billing dispute on Personal Credit Cards is a claim that the cardholder personally makes about one charge already on the account, which must be a purchase, a cash advance or a balance transfer. The agent records the dispute as submitted, dating its notice to the day the cardholder raised it. Disputes about fees, interest or payments are not billing disputes; they are dealt with as fee or interest reversals.

## Notice window

Notice must reach the bank within the notice window, counted from the closing date of the first statement that showed the charge. The clock runs in calendar days from that statement date, as recorded on the charge: the day after the statement date is day 1, and notice is in time when the notice date falls on or before the statement date moved forward by the window's number of days. The window's final day is itself inside the window.

| Tier | Notice window, calendar days after the statement date |
|---|---|
| Secured Visa | 60 |
| College Rewards Visa | 60 |
| Platinum Low Rate Visa | 60 |
| Cash Rewards Visa | 60 |
| Travel Rewards Visa Signature | 60 |
| Visa Infinite Private Client | 60 |

Boundary cases (hypothetical dates): a charge first appears on a statement dated 10 March. Day 1 is 11 March and day 60 is 9 May. Notice given on 9 May is in time; notice given on 10 May is not.

## Temporary credit

- On the day a dispute that meets the notice window is registered, a temporary credit is posted for the amount claimed, capped at the amount of the charge.
- Only a dispute whose status is still submitted can receive a temporary credit, and no dispute receives more than one.
- While the dispute remains open, the disputed amount is left out of the minimum payment, and it accrues neither a late fee nor interest.

## Resolution

| How the dispute ends | Effect |
|---|---|
| In the cardholder's favour, temporary credit already posted | the temporary credit becomes final; nothing new is posted |
| In the cardholder's favour, no temporary credit posted | a final credit is posted on the final dispute ground |
| Either favourable outcome | any fee or interest that the disputed charge gave rise to is taken back |
| Cardholder held liable, or dispute withdrawn | the temporary credit may be rebilled, in full, linked to that temporary credit |

Where the merchant itself refunds the disputed purchase and that refund posts during the life of the dispute, it settles the dispute in the cardholder's favour up to the credit's amount, and the portion of the temporary credit that matches the merchant's refund is rebilled.

> Hypothetical illustration: a 180.00 USD charge is disputed and a 180.00 USD temporary credit posts. The merchant later refunds 70.00 USD while the dispute is open; 70.00 USD of the temporary credit is rebilled, so the cardholder is not credited twice for the same 70.00 USD.
